title: Lesson 76: Auditing Agents: Logs, Replay, Forensics, and Compliance Evidence
description: How an agent audit record must capture every step of a run, why replay turns that record into a reproducible witness, how digital forensics makes it admissible as evidence, and how the same logs demonstrate compliance.

questions.question: An operator plans to reproduce a past agent run by setting temperature to zero and re-running it. Why does this fail?
options: Sampling is only one step, and the logits that feed it are not bit-identical run to run
Temperature zero disables all tool calls, so the re-run halts on its first tool invocation immediately
Setting temperature to zero stops trace capture, so nothing is recorded on the re-run
Every inference provider forbids temperature zero for agent workloads in production
questions.explanation: Temperature controls only the sampling step, while the logits behind it vary with batch composition and hardware numerics. A run therefore cannot be reproduced by running it again; it must be reconstructed from the record.

questions.question: How does deterministic replay reconstruct a past agent run?
options: It re-runs the agent live against current models and compares the new output
It feeds the recorded interactions back in sequence, with stubs replacing live calls
It relies on the model provider's cache to return the same tokens when given the same prompt again
It lowers the sampling temperature until the model stabilizes on a single answer
questions.explanation: Replay does not re-invoke the model or tools. It substitutes proxy stubs that return the recorded responses in the exact original sequence, turning the log into a reproducible witness.

questions.question: How do you prove that an exported agent trace was not altered since it was written?
options: Replay the run live and show that the current output matches the original output
Trust the log because it lives on an append-only store that the agent itself can never rewrite or alter
Ask the engineer who restored the system to confirm that nothing was changed
Recompute the trace's message digest and compare it to the hash stored out of band at write time
questions.explanation: Integrity hashing records a digest of the trace when it is collected and stores it where it cannot change. Re-hashing later and matching proves the record is unaltered, since a single changed bit yields a different digest.
